title: Urban Reconstruction and Population Redistribution: Evidence from Tokyo after the Great Kanto Earthquake
abstract: arXiv:2607.02978v4 Announce Type: replace  Abstract: This study examines the impact of the 1923 Great Kanto Earthquake on population distribution within Tokyo City. The earthquake triggered massive fires that devastated nearly half of the city, including much of its urban core. To investigate its consequences, I digitized systematic census statistics and conducted regression analyses using variation in fire damage across areas. The results show that land readjustment implemented as part of the reconstruction project reduced residential land area within the burned area, leading to higher unit rents. Although the total residential floor area eventually recovered through the construction of multi-story dwellings, the number of households in the burned area remained below its pre-earthquake level throughout the period examined, and the population, while almost recovering by 1935, never exceeded its pre-earthquake level. translated_title: 城市重建与人口再分布：来自关东大地震后东京的证据
translated_abstract: 本研究考察了1923年关东大地震对东京市内人口分布的影响。地震引发的大火摧毁了城市近一半的区域，其中包括大部分城市核心地带。为了研究其后果，作者将系统性的人口普查统计资料数字化，并利用各地区之间火灾破坏程度的差异进行回归分析。结果表明，作为重建项目一部分而实施的土地整理减少了烧毁区域的住宅用地面积，导致单位租金上涨。尽管住宅总建筑面积最终通过多层住宅的建设得以恢复，但在所考察的整个时期内，烧毁区域的家庭户数始终低于震前水平；人口虽然到1935年几乎恢复，但从未超过震前水平。此外，震前建立的分区制度所产生的影响……（原文摘要在此处被截断）
tldr: 该研究利用1923年关东大地震火灾破坏程度的空间差异，发现重建中的土地整理减少了东京烧毁区的住宅用地并推高了租金，致使该区域的户数和人口长期未能恢复到震前水平，从而揭示了灾害后城市重建政策对城市人口再分布的持久性影响。
en_tdlr: Exploiting spatial variation in fire damage from the 1923 Great Kanto Earthquake, this study shows that land readjustment during Tokyo's reconstruction reduced residential land and raised rents in the burned area, leaving its number of households and population permanently below pre-earthquake levels.
